FIND: At [dynamic_management.py#L5304](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5304), `process_round()` feeds the immune layer a system-level `mu` via `marginal_value(round_idx)`. But the actual stop logic uses per-model aggregation through [dynamic_management.py#L2218](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2218), [dynamic_management.py#L2242](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2242), and [dynamic_management.py#L2414](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2414). So Area 7 diagnoses `mu` pathologies on a different metric from the one Area 5 actually uses to stop. I confirmed this with a local probe on the same detector state: `system_mu = 0.1`, `agg_mu = 1.0`, `smoothed_mu = 3.0`.

FIX:
```python
<<<<
mu = self.diminishing_returns.marginal_value(round_idx) if round_idx in self.diminishing_returns._cumulative_yields else 0.0
====
mu = (
    self.diminishing_returns.aggregate_per_model_mu(round_idx)
    if self.diminishing_returns._per_model_yields
    else (
        self.diminishing_returns.marginal_value(round_idx)
        if round_idx in self.diminishing_returns._cumulative_yields
        else 0.0
    )

>>>>
```

FOLLOW: This changes every downstream `mu`-based immune check in `DetectorHealthMonitor.record_round()` and also changes what gets snapshotted by `_get_current_metric("mu")`. The important consequence is good: remediation verification, regression logging, and `mu` pathology detection all start observing the same basis as the stop predicate. A regression test should assert that the immune `mu` equals `aggregate_per_model_mu()` whenever per-model rounds exist.
